findings.title: cmd_set supersede depends on decision order
findings.note: Traced: line 514 only supersedes when the ref is accepted/resolved at set time; the code follows the D2 transition table (story.md:241) literally, so the gap is in the spec. The opposite order supersedes correctly.
findings.reproduces_when: round 2 add with checks STILL-PRESENT F-001 + element FLIP-FLOP F-001 (F-001 -> open, F-002 created); set F-002 accepted (F-001 is open, not in _LIVE, nothing superseded) then set F-001 accepted; check-round passes with both accepted

findings.title: _superseder follows only one step of a supersede chain
findings.note: Downgrade path confirmed. The correct target is debatable: F-003 restates A, so re-raising A agrees with F-003 and is not a flip-flop. The verifier's 'most recent non-superseded' rule should also cite F-003, not F-001.
findings.reproduces_when: F-001 accepted; F-002 = FLIP-FLOP F-001 accepted (F-001 superseded); F-003 = FLIP-FLOP F-002 accepted (F-002 superseded); round 4 sends REOPENS F-001 -> _superseder finds no live F-y -> new-downgraded (line 358-359)

findings.title: No CLI recovery from a committed-unfinished ledger
findings.note: Designed behaviour: D4 step 1 (story.md:354) says STOP and the user resolves it. Reachable only when the ledger is committed outside the protocol, which commits only after check-round passes.
findings.reproduces_when: ledger committed (clean vs HEAD) with a finding in state open: start-round exits 1 at line 192 and set/add exit 1 at line 157

findings.title: start-round discard ignores git checkout/rm return codes
findings.reproduces_when: dirty ledger present and the worktree index.lock exists: git checkout HEAD -- <ledger> fails silently, discarded:true is reported, load() at line 186 reads the dirty round (false 'committed unfinished' or a new round stacked on it)

findings.title: DUPLICATE escalation compares reported vs effective severity
findings.note: The code matches D2's literal wording (story.md:295-297), so the fix needs a spec change too. Each new F-ID lands in Dropped-by-verifier: churn, not a wrong fix.
findings.reproduces_when: round 1 must-fix with demote (effective nice-to-have) rejected --by verifier; round 2 same must-fix + demote with DUPLICATE F-001 -> rank 2 > 0 -> new-downgraded, a new F-ID every round

findings.title: Non-string checks[].ref raises an uncaught TypeError
findings.reproduces_when: add with checks: [{"ref": ["F-001"], "status": "RESOLVED", "evidence": "x:1"}] -> unhashable list in set membership -> traceback, no {"error"} JSON (main catches only LedgerError, line 635)

findings.title: promote accepted with REFUTED verdict or without reproduces_when
findings.note: Line 301 matches D2's validation list (story.md:282-283), which does not require a scenario for promote; REFUTED+promote is harmless at triage (the Dropped bucket wins). Only the null-scenario case matters.
findings.reproduces_when: verified-mode nice-to-have with verdict CONFIRMED, reproduces_when null, severity_action promote -> passes validation (line 307 checks only the reported severity) and becomes a should-fix Blocking row without a scenario

findings.title: show --head is never validated
findings.note: Low impact: the only caller is the orchestrator, which passes the head start-round already validated, and null means unknown per the spec. Option injection needs a caller that already has a shell.
findings.reproduces_when: show --head deadbeef (every decided finding gets file_changed null via git exit 128), or --head=--output=/tmp/x passed as a git diff argument before '--' at lines 539/544

findings.title: OpenCode bash allow-list lacks review_ledger.py
findings.note: Already covered by the existing "python scripts/qs/*": allow rule (qs-review-task.md.j2:56, qs-verify-task.md.j2:57).

findings.title: file_changed cat-file pre-check not stated in D2
findings.note: The deviation protects against a false 'unchanged' that would wrongly turn a re-raise into a DUPLICATE. Documenting it in D2 is the cheaper resolution.
findings.reproduces_when: a decided finding whose where path exists at neither revision (e.g. a bare 'charger.py:2471'): the code returns null, while D2 (story.md:324-325) maps git diff exit 0 to false

findings.title: load validates only the top-level shape
_md does not escape newlines in cells
duplicate history note records pre-reconcile state
findings.note: The note is appended before the later transition note in the same add, so the history stays in order; not stale.

findings.title: no lock or atomic write; concurrent set calls lose a decision
findings.note: Not promoted: a lost set leaves its finding open, and check-round (step 8) catches that and sends it back to triage.

findings.title: add does not enforce that the verifier returned every consolidated finding
findings.note: add has no input listing the consolidated keys, so it cannot detect a missing one. The verifier prompt says add rejects this case, but it does not.
findings.reproduces_when: consolidated C-1+C-2, verifier object lists only C-1 -> _validate checks duplicate keys only, add exits 0, C-2 never enters the ledger (the verifier template at qs-review-finding-verifier.md.j2:134 claims add rejects this)

findings.title: Verify findings against the PR head, not the local worktree
findings.note: No clean-worktree check exists in the review templates. The precondition (a dirty worktree at review time) is rare, and the reviewers that read the repo have the same exposure.
findings.reproduces_when: worktree has an uncommitted edit to a file a finding cites when the round opens; only HEAD SHAs are compared, and the verifier reads the edited file and can REFUTE a defect still present at the head

findings.title: Fast-path condition in phase-protocols.md omits bucket precedence
findings.note: The doc wording is loose. The rendered orchestrator template is exact: it excludes FLIP-FLOP and Reopened findings (_macros.md.j2:333-335), so runtime behaviour is unaffected.

history.note: user: override verifier default: cheap doc gap (delegated)

findings.title: phase-protocols.md does not describe the all-skipped round completion
findings.note: Doc-only gap. The template covers this path: ledger-only commit plus finish-task handoff (qs-review-task.md.j2:273-284).

history.note: user: override verifier default: cheap doc gap (delegated)

findings.title: review_open_round fetches gh pr diff before the push when local is ahead
findings.note: The reviewers fetch the diff themselves later, so they are not affected (qs-review-task.md.j2:110). Only a diff pasted to the verifier would be stale.
findings.reproduces_when: local head ahead of the PR head (an earlier push failed), full round: step 1's gh pr diff output predates the git push at line 216-217, and the orchestrator passes it to the verifier as the diff for this round

findings.title: Out-of-scope changes: Claude frontier model change and stale.yml test removal
findings.note: The story scopes the model change (D7, AC-10 at story.md:556). The stale.yml test was changed because main deleted the workflow in 9db87a91 (tests/qs/test_github_workflows.py:24-27), so CI needs it.

findings.title: Fallback-mode validation accepts checks, demote and non-NEW relations
findings.note: Defence in depth: the template's fallback object always has checks [], keep and NEW (_macros.md.j2:297-301), but the CLI does not enforce that.
findings.reproduces_when: a fallback object with checks [RESOLVED F-001] plus a finding with severity_action demote and relation DUPLICATE F-002 -> passes _validate (only a non-null verdict is rejected at line 334-335), F-001 is marked resolved and the finding is suppressed as a duplicate, with nothing verified

findings.title: verdict REFUTED with relation REOPENS reopens F-x and defaults to fix
findings.note: Neither the validator nor the verifier prompt forbids pairing REFUTED with REOPENS.
findings.reproduces_when: verifier emits verdict REFUTED, relation REOPENS F-001 for an accepted F-001 -> _resolve targets F-001 whatever the verdict, _reconcile reopens it with effect reopened, and triage row 2 (Reopened, default fix) wins over row 4 (Dropped by verifier)

findings.title: create-plan lane rows can no longer tell a lane-aware render from the no-lane fallback
findings.note: No effort assertion separates the two cases either, since CLASS_EFFORT gives both deep and frontier 'high'.
findings.reproduces_when: a regression where build_payload drops lane before models.resolve -> every create-plan row still expects claude-opus-5-5 and passes, because frontier == deep on Claude (models.py:50-51) and both have effort high (models.py:78-79)

findings.title: Ledger-state summary omits open -> superseded
findings.note: Story D2 was updated (story.md:241) but this summary was not. The source is scenario-exempt, so no demote.

findings.title: Second fail("set") repeats the first; the no-round case is never run
Story should state DUPLICATE elements are never reported as merged
review_decisions does not handle set exit 1 after an in-round supersede
findings.note: This follows from fix #01 F-001 (open -> superseded). The F-001 fix itself works; the template was not updated to handle it.
findings.reproduces_when: F-001 accepted in round 1; round 2 has a STILL-PRESENT check on F-001 plus a FLIP-FLOP F-001 element (creates F-0xx); the user fixes F-0xx and picks fix all; set F-0xx supersedes F-001 (line 561), then set F-001 exits 1 'superseded' and review_decisions (_macros.md.j2:383-401) has no branch for it

findings.title: stale_fix_plans misses a staged-but-uncommitted fix plan
findings.reproduces_when: step 8 git add succeeds, git commit fails, then start-round runs: ls-files --others skips the staged fix plan, so it is not reported, and next_review_fix_path (utils.py:196-201) counts it and skips its number

findings.title: Committed-unfinished recovery sets are discarded by a premature start-round
findings.note: It only happens if the orchestrator skips the commit that the template asks for before restarting. The lost decisions can be redone.
findings.reproduces_when: committed ledger has open F-001 and F-002; set F-001 accepted (ledger now dirty); start-round runs before the commit -> the dirty ledger is checked out from HEAD and the run fails 'committed unfinished' again with discarded:true, and the exit-1 bullet (_macros.md.j2:235-239) never says the decisions were lost

findings.title: check-round exits 0 for a started round that was never added
findings.note: It requires an orchestrator to deviate from the protocol. --force-full can still open a new round.
findings.reproduces_when: the orchestrator skips add and runs check-round -> exit 0 (no added/started check); once committed, start-round on the same head returns no-change (line 222-224), and add on the now-clean ledger fails

findings.title: no-change branch guidance contradicts discarded:true and omits unimplemented accepted fixes
review_record never says what to pass to the required --keys when consolidation produced no findings
findings.note: A gap in how F-015's fix is documented, not in its logic: `--keys ""` (or `--keys=`) works but is never mentioned. F-015 itself is checked RESOLVED.
findings.reproduces_when: a round with zero consolidated findings (it still runs add, for the checks) where the orchestrator copies _macros.md.j2:329 with an empty key list, giving a bare `--keys`: argparse rejects it as usage exit 1, and the template then blames the verifier's object, so the round falls back, dropping every check

findings.title: Test helper builds --keys with duplicates, so _validate's duplicate-finding-key branch is no longer tested
findings.note: No other test sends duplicate finding keys, so the _validate branch has no test. The helper should dedupe the keys, or the case should pass --keys=C-1.
findings.reproduces_when: _VALIDATION_CASES['duplicate_finding_key'] runs through led.fail('add') with no explicit --keys: the helper passes --keys=C-1,C-1, add exits at '--keys lists a key twice', and the _validate duplicate branch is never reached

findings.title: seen_keys may be undefined in the new key-set check
findings.note: seen_keys is set unconditionally at line 340, before the findings loop. The check at line 382 always sees it, even for an empty findings list.

findings.title: Committed-unfinished guard indexes rounds[-1] without checking rounds is non-empty
findings.note: A regression in the new F-029 guard. Before the delta, a deleted working ledger was restored from HEAD. The trigger is narrow, but the crash is real.
findings.reproduces_when: HEAD holds a committed-unfinished ledger and the working copy is deleted (_dirty true) or rewritten with rounds []: load() returns empty rounds, working['rounds'][-1] raises IndexError, and main catches only LedgerError, so you get a traceback instead of a JSON error

findings.title: Corrupt working copy under a committed-unfinished HEAD now exits 2 instead of being restored
findings.note: Before fix #02 the dirty copy was checked out from HEAD first, so this state recovered by itself.
findings.reproduces_when: HEAD ledger is committed-unfinished and the working ledger is truncated or invalid JSON: load() raises LedgerError(2) before the discard, and the macro says HALT on exit 2 without giving any recovery

findings.title: Findings accepted during committed-unfinished recovery never reach a fix plan
findings.note: Related to F-031 (default-skipped), but the recovery bullet changed since that decision, so it counts as NEW. With --force-full the verifier would check F-001 STILL-PRESENT. Without it, the fix is silently lost.
findings.reproduces_when: round N committed with F-001 open; set F-001 accepted (decided_round = N); check-round reports accepted_unchecked [] since decided_round == n; ledger-only commit; restart at step 1 on the same code head: start-round returns no-change, the template stops, and no fix plan is ever written for F-001

findings.title: --keys entries are stripped but finding keys are compared raw
Story drift: D1/D4 do not record fix #02's F-016, F-019, F-015, F-022, F-027; stale Status line
findings.note: D4 step 1 has no git status check and does not fetch the diff after the sync. Step 5 has no --keys and step 8 has no FLIP-FLOP-first rule. The D1 relations lack the REFUTED rule. The Status line is stale.

findings.title: AC-14 is a process criterion; CI shard 1/4 still pending
findings.note: A process check that the code cannot settle: confirm CI is green before finish-task.

findings.title: `except ValueError, LedgerError:` (PEP 758) is a SyntaxError on Python <=3.13
findings.note: Project targets Python 3.14 only (mypy 3.14, ruff py314, CI python-version 3.14); PEP 758 syntax is valid there.

findings.title: Deleted working copy: load() may raise FileNotFoundError, uncaught
findings.note: load() returns an empty ledger for a missing path and never raises; the rounds mismatch sends it down the restore path; the parametrized 'deleted' test covers it.

findings.title: Recovery bullet says 'finish that round exactly like step 8' but {{round}} is unbound on that path
findings.note: Low impact: N is in the error string. One clause ('{{round}} = N from the error') closes it.
findings.reproduces_when: start-round exits 1 'round 3 committed unfinished'; the user accepts a recovery decision; the orchestrator reaches the step-8 fix-plan 'Review round' line and commit message using {{round}}, which only the success bullet binds

findings.title: Recovery branches on 'any recovery decision accepted', dropping findings accepted in round N before the stray commit
findings.note: Adjacent case of F-037. Branch on 'any finding accepted with decided_round N'.
findings.reproduces_when: step 8 sets F-004 accepted (decided_round N); a stray commit captures the ledger with F-005 open; recovery skips F-005, so the all-skipped branch runs: ledger-only commit, restart, no-change, and check-round does not list F-004 (decided_round == n), so F-004 never gets a fix plan

findings.title: stale_fix_plans 'delete' advice conflicts with a recovery fix plan whose commit failed
Malformed finding entry gives KeyError/TypeError in _recovery_copy
findings.note: Same class as F-011 (default-skipped). The region changed, so it counts as NEW.
